column1: # Constructs bash 3.2 does not have, one per row: name<TAB>regex<TAB>sample violation.
# The list is MEASURED, not remembered. Every row was run under /bin/bash (3.2.57, what
# macOS ships) and under Homebrew bash 5.3.9 and the two were compared on stdout, stderr
# and exit status; only constructs that DIVERGED are here. The probe and its output are in
# Four of them diverge SILENTLY — 3.2 exits 0, writes nothing to stderr, and produces a
# different answer. That is why this file exists at all and why running the script under a
# real 3.2 is not by itself a gate:
#   {1..9..2}      3.2 prints the literal `{1..9..2}`         5 prints `1 3 5 7 9`
#   $SRANDOM       3.2: unset                                 5: set
#   $EPOCHSECONDS  3.2: unset                                 5: set
#   $EPOCHREALTIME 3.2: unset                                 5: set
# and two more exit 0 with only a line on stderr, which a script without `set -e` swallows:
#   declare -A m   3.2: `declare: -A: invalid option`, then m is an INDEXED array
#   mapfile        3.2: `mapfile: command not found`
# The regex column is an awk ERE, matched per line against source with full-line comments
# removed. It carries no backslashes: it is used as a dynamic regex, where a backslash
# would have to be doubled and the doubling is the kind of thing that is got wrong once and
# then never looked at again.
# The sample column is not decoration. tools/bash-compat-lint.sh plants each sample into a
# fixture on every run and asserts the scan finds it, finds it EXACTLY once, and finds
# nothing in a clean fixture — the three observations doc:50-memory-and-evidence#evidence-kinds
# requires of a mechanism claiming to discriminate. A row whose sample stops matching, or
# starts matching two rules, fails the gate here rather than quietly widening or narrowing it.
# This is a DENYLIST and therefore fails open: a bash 4 feature nobody has named passes.
# doc:00-constitution#observed-failing says as much about enumerating shapes. It is here
# because the alternative — the interpreter — fails open on the two constructs bean:0049
# names by name, which is worse. The complementary half is the `-n` parse under the pinned
# interpreter, which does fail closed and catches every SYNTAX-level bash 4 feature,
# including ones absent from this file. Neither half subsumes the other.
# Adding a row: run it under both interpreters first, and put a row here only if they
# disagree. A construct both accept is not a compatibility rule, it is a style preference.
associative-array
nameref
mapfile
case-modification
parameter-transform
append-both-streams
pipe-both-streams
case-fallthrough
coproc
shopt-bash4-option
brace-expansion-step
negative-subscript
test-v
wait-n
printf-time-format
bash4-variable
